result:
A race condition is a bug where the result depends on the unpredictable timing of two or more processes touching the same thing at once. With a shared log file, two scripts' writes can interleave, or one can overwrite the other's.

To avoid it, always append with `>>` (never `>`), and take a lock around the write so only one process writes at a time:

```sh
(
  flock 9
  printf '%s %s\n' "$(date -Is)" "$msg" >> "$LOG"
) 9>"$LOG.lock"
```

Every writer must use the same lock file, and the lock is released automatically when the subshell exits, even on a crash.

A single short `printf ... >> "$LOG"` line is in practice safe without the lock on a local filesystem, because append-mode writes land whole at the end of the file. The lock is needed once an entry spans multiple lines or commands.

`flock` is not reliable on NFS; if the log lives there, send entries through `logger` to syslog instead.
